sections.risk_rationale: Guideline mandates a personal story of encountering the static-knowledge problem plus open-book exam/human cheat-sheet analogies and Lesson 10 contrasts that extend beyond cited sources' mainly technical descriptions.

Purely descriptive decomposition into retrieval/augmentation/generation pillars plus Mermaid diagram; closely matches technical foundations in sources such as a-complete-guide-to-rag with no normative leaps.
End-to-end pipeline steps with example tools/models are technical and descriptive; sources supply direct matches for ingestion/retrieval phases and diagrams, keeping interpretive weight low.

Guideline dictates multiple specific invented scenarios (e.g. "my bill keeps rolling over" hybrid example, travel-policy decomposition, reimbursements handbook chunking, retail/IT GraphRAG multi-hop queries) as illustrative narratives.

Fully scripted mini thought-process example with verbatim Thought/Action/Observation steps plus analogies to a "research assistant" and ReAct-tool integration carry interpretive weight relative to source support.

Normative/evaluative claims that RAG is "the most used solution," a "foundational competency," and that "the future of knowledge retrieval is agentic" plus positioning within Context Engineering exceed purely descriptive source coverage.

parsed.overall_notes: RAG is a highly canonical, oversaturated topic (high topic_canonicity) with largely independent sources from diverse vendors and an arXiv paper, though many restate core concepts. Dominant signal is elevated scripted-example fractions in S4 and S5 from guideline-dictated illustrative scenarios, paired with moderate argumentative risk in framing, analogies, and normative positioning in S1/S5/S6.
